note: Attacker-controlled *MATERIAL_COUNT token of the second *MATERIAL_LIST block is parsed as unsigned int 4294967295 (0xFFFFFFFF), the maximum value, with no upper-bound validation.
Old material count captured at entry of the second *MATERIAL_LIST block is 1, because the first *MATERIAL_LIST block already resized m_vMaterials to hold one material.

The unsigned 32-bit sum 1 + 4294967295 wraps to 0, so m_vMaterials is resized to 0 elements while the logical index space (iMaterialCount = 4294967295) stays huge - the allocation is shrunk below the logical index space.
Material index 0 is parsed; the guard `iIndex >= iMaterialCount` (0 >= 4294967295) is false, so the out-of-range check passes and execution continues.
Out-of-bounds read of invalid object state: m_vMaterials has 0 elements but index 0 + 1 = 1 is dereferenced; sMat becomes a reference to invalid memory.
ParseLV2MaterialBlock is invoked on the invalid material; *NUMSUBMTLS triggers submaterial-vector reallocation on the garbage avSubMaterials vector, reading invalid object state and crashing.
